data.title: Scope Creep
data.tagline: New requests continually enter agreed project work without being evaluated
data.learningOutcome: You can compare the agreed work with the actual page, keep the requested change, and identify what should be reverted or evaluated separately.
data.description: You ask AI to make the login button blue, then notice that the header and card shadow changed too. Those changes were never discussed, yet they have entered this delivery. A new request can become part of the scope after it is recorded and evaluated; scope creep is the unassessed addition of work to the current plan.

learning.assumes: You have seen a project grow beyond plan, or had AI make changes you did not ask for.
learning.outcome: You can compare the agreed work with the actual page, keep the requested change, and identify what should be reverted or evaluated separately.

distinctions.label: Requirement change
distinctions.explanation: A requirement change formally adjusts scope after evaluation and syncs everyone; scope creep adds requirements without evaluation.

distinctions.label: Backlog
distinctions.explanation: Backlog items are queued and not yet decided; scope creep is the part already being done that exceeds the agreed scope.

explanation.title: Compare the actual result
explanation.text: Compare the agreement with the page and change record. An edit elsewhere is not automatically wrong, but it should not silently enter this delivery.

explanation.title: Evaluate real changes separately
explanation.text: A needed request can join the scope after it is recorded and evaluated with a new delivery and acceptance plan.

data.boundary: Scope creep is not every scope adjustment. A discussed, recorded, and evaluated request is a controlled change; the concern is new work slipping into the current plan without that decision.

lessonPractice.title: You ask AI to change a button color, and it also changes the card shadow and the page title size. What should happen?

options.label: Compare with the original page, undo the title and shadow edits, then accept the blue button
options.feedback: Correct. The request covered only the button color; restore the other two changes and keep the requested result.

options.label: Keep all three changes for now, then decide later which ones to deliver
options.feedback: That leaves the unreviewed title and shadow edits inside this delivery, so it still does not match the agreed scope.

options.label: Restore the button, title, and shadow to their original appearance
options.feedback: That also removes the requested blue button. Only the two unrequested changes need review.

data.agentPrompt: Change only the login button to blue. Afterward, compare the page and change list to confirm the header and cards were not changed along the way. If another area really needs an update, explain why first.

references.title: Scope creep ... not necessarily a bad thing
